import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths as given
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/training_7.csv"
]

# Target schema columns in order
target_columns = [
    'movie_display_name',
    'movie_production_year',
    'movie_genre_display_name',
    'movie_financial_summary_production_budget',
    'movie_financial_summary_international_box_office',
    'movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold',
    'movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units',
    'movie_acting_role_display_name',
    'movie_theatrical_release_release_date',
    'movie_creative_type_display_name',
    'movie_production_method_display_name',
    'movie_source_display_name',
    'movie_running_time',
    'movie_technical_role_display_name',
    'movie_production_company_display_name',
    'movie_sequel'
]

# Data types for target columns (to ensure consistency)
# Using pandas dtypes approximations
dtype_map = {
    'movie_display_name': 'string',
    'movie_production_year': 'Int64',  # nullable integer
    'movie_genre_display_name': 'string',
    'movie_financial_summary_production_budget': 'Int64',
    'movie_financial_summary_international_box_office': 'Int64',
    'movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold': 'float',
    'movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units': 'float',
    'movie_acting_role_display_name': 'string',
    'movie_theatrical_release_release_date': 'string',  # keep as string (ISO date)
    'movie_creative_type_display_name': 'string',
    'movie_production_method_display_name': 'string',
    'movie_source_display_name': 'string',
    'movie_running_time': 'float',
    'movie_technical_role_display_name': 'string',
    'movie_production_company_display_name': 'string',
    'movie_sequel': 'Int64'
}

# Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema (all source schemas are identical)
    # Reorder columns to target_columns order (they are already in that order in sources)
    df = df[target_columns]

    # Convert columns to target dtypes carefully
    # For integer columns with possible NaNs, use pandas nullable Int64 dtype
    for col, dtype in dtype_map.items():
        if dtype == 'Int64':
            # Convert to nullable integer
            df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
        elif dtype == 'float':
            df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)
        elif dtype == 'string':
            # Convert to string, keep NaNs as pd.NA
            df[col] = df[col].astype('string')
        else:
            # fallback: no conversion
            pass

    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we can union (concatenate) all source DataFrames
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Final check: ensure columns order and dtypes again (safe)
target_df = target_df[target_columns]
for col, dtype in dtype_map.items():
    if dtype == 'Int64':
        target_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(target_df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
    elif dtype == 'float':
        target_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(target_df[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)
    elif dtype == 'string':
        target_df[col] = target_df[col].astype('string')

# Write the final target DataFrame to the specified CSV path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_93/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
